input.question: Is the Russian economy actually collapsing? And if so, what's causing the collapse?
input.ground_truth: Money... or more precisely, lack of it. It is estimated that Russian investors (let alone foreign investors) have moved billions of dollars out of Russia as a result of the political turmoil created by the Ukraine situation. If you take huge amount of capital out of an economy, the effects will be felt throughout: banks might become insolvent, people and businesses won't be able to take loans, other businesses won't be able to sell their products, etc. It's a chain reaction that ends up affecting the entire economy. The last couple of weeks have been particularly hard on Russia also because of the oil price being very low lately. One of Russia's main revenue sources is energy exports. Well, if you cannot make profits on energy sales, that's not good... I believe that's one reason the Russian ruble took such a beating the other day... Edit: Just found this: _URL_0_

Question: Is the Russian economy actually collapsing? And if so, what's causing the collapse?

Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box full of toys. That toy box is like a country's economy. Now, Russia's toy box was once really big and had lots of cool toys. But lately, some things are happening that are making it hard for them to keep so many toys.

First, some of the kids (other countries) who used to trade toys with Russia don't want to play with them anymore because they're upset with Russia. So, Russia can't get as many new toys or sell as many of their old ones.

Also, it's getting more expensive for Russia to make new toys because the stuff to make toys with (like oil and other materials) isn't as easy to get or costs more money.

On top of that, some of the toys in the box are broken or not as fun as before, so people don't want them. This makes Russia's toy box seem smaller and less fun than before.

So, even though Russia still has a lot of toys, it's getting harder for them to keep the toy box full and happy. That's what people mean when they say the Russian economy is "collapsing"—it's like their toy box is starting to lose toys and not get as many new ones.
